title: Who Should Grade My Work? Student Perspectives on Transparent AI-Assisted Writing Assessment in Higher Education
abstract: arXiv:2609.05346v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The integration of GenAI tools into higher education assessment raises important questions about how students understand, interpret, and respond to AI-mediated evaluation. As instructors increasingly explore AI tools for providing feedback, prior research has examined whether GenAI-generated feedback improves writing performance and how students perceive its usefulness; comparatively little is known, however, about how students interpret such evaluation when they are explicitly informed that an AI system, rather than a human instructor, produced the feedback and the score. This study reports findings from a qualitative pedagogical inquiry conducted in an undergraduate technical communication course for computing students at a Saudi public university. translated_title: 谁应该为我的作业评分？高等教育中透明AI辅助写作评估的学生视角
translated_abstract: 将生成式AI（GenAI）工具融入高等教育评估引发了重要问题：学生如何理解、解读并回应由AI中介的评估。随着教师日益探索使用AI工具提供反馈，已有研究考察了GenAI生成的反馈能否提升写作表现以及学生如何感知其有用性；然而，关于当学生被明确告知反馈与评分由AI系统（而非人类教师）产生时，他们如何解读此类评估，目前所知相对较少。本研究报告了一项质性教学探究的结果，该研究在沙特一所公立大学面向计算机专业本科生的技术传播课程中开展。十三名男性计算机专业本科生完成了一项课堂手写写作任务；扫描后的作业提交由ChatGPT依据基于评分量规的提示进行评估，该提示与（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本研究首次在透明披露评估来源的前提下开展质性研究，揭示了当计算机专业本科生明确知晓ChatGPT（而非人类教师）为其写作评分时，他们如何理解和回应这种AI辅助写作评估。
en_tdlr: This qualitative study reveals how undergraduate computing students interpret and respond to transparent AI-assisted writing assessment when explicitly informed that ChatGPT, rather than a human instructor, produced the feedback and scores.
